newsitem.title: USA: CBOT corn ends lower on soy slide, commercials.
newsitem.headline: CBOT corn ends lower on soy slide, commercials.

text.p: CBOT corn futures closed mostly lower on a drop in soybeans plus commercial selling, traders said.
Cargill Inc sold 5.5 million bushels of December and Farmers Commodities Corp sold 2.5 million bushels of December, traders said.
Long liquidation in the July weighed on that month relative to the other contracts, the traders said.
Traders said the corn market continued to labor under the weight of only routine exports and on U.S. Midwest weather that is nearly ideal for crop development.

Continental Grain did 3.5 million bushels of December/July at 22 to 21-1/2 cents, premium July, traders said. E.D. and F. Man Interntional spread five million bushels of July/December at 20-1/2 to 21-1/2 cents, premium July, traders said.
Tenco Inc spread three million bushels of Dec/July and SAK Futures did three million Dec/July, traders said.
Corn futures closed 3-3/4 cents per bushel lower to one cent higher, with July down 3-3/4 at $2.66-1/2 a bushel. December ended 3-1/2 cents lower at $2.45-1/4.
Corn futures volume was estimated by the CBOT at 83,000 contracts, above the actual 70,983 traded Tuesday.

In corn options, Cargill Investor Services sold 600 September $2.70 calls at 4-3/4 cents, Goldenberg Hehmeyer sold 800 December $2.40 calls at 15 cents and LIT America sold 500 July $2.60 puts at 3/8 cent, traders said.
Corn options volume was estimated at 15,000 contracts, below the 16,036 traded Tuesday.
